audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Gnar/Skill/Yone/Yone/Gnar/Yone/Yone. Packet says Gnar,Gnar,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Yone and the whys[] prose agrees with the packet on all five disputed stages.
audit.why: whys[1] says the level-2 chunk is one 'his melee Q can't punish yet' — that is a Gnar stage, marked Skill. whys[2] literally ends 'a wash' — marked Yone. whys[3] and whys[5] both describe genuinely two-sided stages ('strong if... a liability if', 'trades evenly') — both marked Yone. whys[4] says the level-6 window is 'purely whether Mega is up', which is Skill, not Gnar. Only whys[6] and level 1 currently match their enum.
audit.corrected: Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Yone, proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer spike text said 'Stridebreaker'; Yone's real spike structure is Soul Unbound's cooldown decay and his two-item crit timing.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1 but 10s at rank 5 — that halving is the single biggest change in this lane, because 'bait E, then commit' stops being a plan once it is back up in ten seconds. Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1, long enough to play whole waves around. Neither number was on the page.
audit.corrected: Phase whys and the cooldown block now carry Soul Unbound's 22s-to-10s decay and Fate Sealed's 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Fate Sealed a KNOCKUP in three places (whys[4], spikes[2].text, mid). Riot's description says he blinks behind the last champion in a line and PULLS all enemies hit towards him, and the kit carries no knockup flag on his R.
audit.why: The distinction changes the play. A knockup would be airborne CC you cannot act through; a pull is a displacement toward him, which means the danger is being dragged out of Boomerang range into his W cleave, not being locked in the air. A Gnar reading 'knockup' will hold Wallop expecting to be stunned and instead find himself repositioned.
audit.corrected: Corrected all three to a blink-behind-and-pull, and stated it explicitly in dontsFull[2].d and the cooldown block so the page cannot drift back.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d described Soul Unbound with no number at all, and the whole full layer omitted Spirit Cleave.
audit.why: Spirit Cleave is a 14s shield whose cooldown and cast time scale with his attack speed — it gets faster as he builds, which is exactly why late trades that 'should' work do not. The page never mentions it outside a boilerplate title.
audit.corrected: Added Spirit Cleave's 14s and attack-speed scaling, and Mortal Steel's flat 4s.

edits.before: This is the volatile stretch and it's pure Rage RNG. If Mega is up, bait his E out by feinting an engage, then land a Wallop line-stun (or a wall-GNAR!) on the rewind and you can kill him. If you're stuck in Mini with Rage down, his stacked-Q dash-in plus W cleave and the level-6 R knockup shred your squishy body, so never facecheck a fight without checking your bar first. The lane swings entirely on which form you're in when he commits.
edits.after: This is the volatile stretch and it's pure Rage RNG. If Mega is up, bait his E out by feinting an engage, then land a Wallop line-stun (or a wall-GNAR!) on the rewind — Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1, so that punish window is real. If you're stuck in Mini with Rage down, his stacked-Q dash-in plus W cleave and the level-6 Fate Sealed pull shred your squishy body. The lane swings entirely on which form you're in when he commits.

notes: Two real errors fixed. First, the level chart: five of seven stages contradicted their own whys[] text, including whys[2] which literally ends 'a wash' while the enum said Yone wins. Second, the page called Fate Sealed a knockup in three separate places — Riot's text says he blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls enemies toward him, and there is no knockup flag on his R. That matters because a pull drags you out of Boomerang range into Spirit Cleave rather than locking you airborne, so the counterplay is different. Also added Spirit Cleave, which the full layer never mentioned once despite being a 14s shield that gets FASTER as he builds attack speed — the reason late trades stop working. I did NOT change the page's 'third Q' phrasing: Riot's text says the empowered cast fires at 2 stacks, which is the third cast, so the page is right. Not verified: whether Mega Wallop's stun applied to Yone's spirit also lands on the body when Soul Unbound snaps back, or only the reverse — the content layer's central plan (whys[3], spikes[1], mid, wants.you[1]) depends on stunning the return, and Riot's text does not describe the CC interaction.
